title: Refund cap is per-approval, not cumulative: two cancellation requests on one booking approve two full refunds (200% of collected funds) in Boarding and Pet Sitting
actor: Two staff identities, real forwarded-identity workspace auth (no preview). Requester: care@pawspace.in, app_users role_code='admin'. Approver: finance.manager@pawspace.in, app_users role_code='finance' (permissions include finance.view, finance.manage). Segregation-of-duties check requester!=approver is satisfied. Not development preview.
request:
POST /api/sitting-finance (app/api/sitting-finance/route.ts -> lib/sitting-finance-governance.ts mutateSittingFinance), four calls in order, each with a distinct idempotencyKey:
1) {bookingId:'BK-1',action:'request_cancel',idempotencyKey:'r-a',reason:'customer travel cancelled'} as care@pawspace.in
2) {bookingId:'BK-1',action:'request_cancel',idempotencyKey:'r-b',reason:'second cancellation request'} as care@pawspace.in
3) {bookingId:'BK-1',action:'approve_cancel',idempotencyKey:'a-1',reason:'full refund approved',approvedRefundAmount:8000} as finance.manager@pawspace.in
4) {bookingId:'BK-1',action:'approve_cancel',idempotencyKey:'a-2',reason:'full refund approved again',approvedRefundAmount:8000} as finance.manager@pawspace.in
then record_refund twice with references RFND-0001 / RFND-0002, then action:'reconcile'.
Identical sequence against lib/boarding-finance-governance.ts mutateBoardingFinance reproduces it for Boarding.
d1_before:
canonical_bookings: id=BK-1, service_code='pet_sitting', status='confirmed', total_amount=8000, customer_id='CUS-1', provider_id='PRV-1', schedule_group_id='SG-1'.
booking_payments: id=PAY-1, booking_id='BK-1', amount=8000, amount_due_now=8000, status='captured', gateway='uat_sandbox'.
No stay_payment_schedules row. lib/collected-funds.ts collectedForBooking(db,'BK-1') = 8000 (verified by direct call).
sitting_cancellation_requests: 0 rows. sitting_refund_ledger: 0 rows.
d1_after:
sitting_cancellation_requests: 2 rows, BOTH status='approved', each approved_refund_amount=8000, each decision_by='finance.manager@pawspace.in'.
sitting_refund_ledger: 2 rows -
  {id:'1fbe33c9-3f3d-406b-877e-07cad74a218a', cancellation_request_id:'0e76b580-...', amount:8000, status:'sandbox_recorded', reference:'RFND-0002'}
  {id:'0cc82fae-d5e7-4d6c-90f0-b9b849f2b2ae', cancellation_request_id:'d745dec3-...', amount:8000, status:'sandbox_recorded', reference:'RFND-0001'}
  SELECT SUM(amount) WHERE status='sandbox_recorded' -> 16000 against 8000 collected.
canonical_bookings.status='cancelled'.
sitting_finance_reconciliation: 1 row {booking_total:8000, captured_amount:8000, refund_total:16000, net_customer_amount:0, status:'attention_required'} - net is clamped by Math.max(0,captured-refundTotal) so the 8000 over-refund reads as 0, not as -8000.
Boarding run: boarding_refund_ledger 2 rows, total 16000 on the same 8000 collected.
repeatable: Yes. Run twice from a clean in-memory D1 via two independent probes: (a) direct lib call to mutateSittingFinance, (b) the real POST /api/sitting-finance route handler with real workspace auth. Both produced 2 ledger rows totalling 16000. The cross-service probe reproduced Boarding (16000) and Sitting (16000) in the same run.
canonical_failure: approve_cancel caps approvedRefundAmount against collectedForBooking() alone and never against refunds already approved for the same booking, and it does not refuse a booking whose status is already 'cancelled', so N open cancellation requests yield N full refunds totalling N x the money actually collected.
contributing_controls: lib/sitting-finance-governance.ts request_cancel has NO guard against a second open cancellation request; lib/boarding-finance-governance.ts likewise. lib/walking-finance-governance.ts and lib/taxi-finance-governance.ts DO carry that guard (SELECT id FROM <svc>_cancellation_requests WHERE booking_id=? AND status='policy_review_required' LIMIT 1), which is why those two are not exposed by this path.
approve_cancel blocks only status=='in_progress'; 'cancelled' is not refused, so the second approval runs on a terminal booking.
The unique index <ledger>_one_refund_per_request is on cancellation_request_id, so two DIFFERENT requests each legitimately own one refund row - the DB floor cannot see the per-booking total.
sitting_finance_reconciliation.net_customer_amount = Math.max(0, captured - refundTotal) hides the negative net that would otherwise expose the over-refund.
blast_radius: Every Boarding and Pet Sitting booking. Any staff member who can raise a cancellation request plus any one finance approver can move an unbounded multiple of the collected amount out of the company per booking (3 requests = 300%). The refund rows are marked sandbox_pending/sandbox_recorded today, so the loss is realised the moment the refund executor is wired to a live gateway; the ledger, the reconciliation row and the finance UI already report the inflated figure as approved.
regression: tests/refund-cap-collected-funds.test.mjs :: "<service>: two cancellation requests cannot approve two full refunds" + "<service>: a partial refund and its remainder still work, but not a rupee past collected" (both run against Boarding AND Pet Sitting)
fix_note: The refund ceiling now belongs to the BOOKING rather than to a single approval: an approval is capped at collectedForBooking() minus the refunds already on this booking's ledger (any status except failed/cancelled). Refund policy is unchanged and a partial refund followed by its remainder still works. The per-request atomic claim already in these modules is a different control - it stops two approvers racing on ONE request, and it worked correctly here, since these were two separate requests each claimed exactly once.
collateral: The regressions live in the existing tests/refund-cap-collected-funds.test.mjs, which fixed WHICH ceiling an approval uses (collected money, not the booking total) but applied it one approval at a time. Its assertRefused helper approves with a default idempotency key, so the new cases deliberately seed under a different key - an idempotent replay would have returned the first approval's success and hidden the defect.

title: A closed and locked period still accepts every finance write: late refund, new invoice, and a manual journal all posted into 2026-07 after closeMonth locked it
actor: Finance staff (finance.manage) and a founder actor. Direct real-lib execution: lib/finance-monthly-close.ts closeMonth as founder@pawspace.in; then lib/sitting-finance-governance.ts mutateSittingFinance as care@pawspace.in (requester) and fin@pawspace.in (approver), lib/sitting-invoice.ts issueSittingInvoice as fin@pawspace.in, lib/finance-accounts.ts postJournal (no actor argument exists at all). Not preview.
request:
1) closeMonth(db,{period:'2026-07',actorId:'founder@pawspace.in'}) after recordBoardApproval('2026-07') made every checklist item green.
Then, with finance_close_periods.period_code='2026-07' status='locked':
A) mutateSittingFinance({bookingId:'BK-A',action:'request_cancel',actorId:'care@pawspace.in',idempotencyKey:'lk-r1',reason:'late cancellation after close'})
B) mutateSittingFinance({bookingId:'BK-A',action:'approve_cancel',actorId:'fin@pawspace.in',idempotencyKey:'lk-a1',reason:'late refund after period close',approvedRefundAmount:10000})
C) mutateSittingFinance({bookingId:'BK-A',action:'record_refund',actorId:'fin@pawspace.in',idempotencyKey:'lk-rr1',reason:'late refund recorded',refundReference:'LATE-0001'})
D) issueSittingInvoice(db,{bookingId:'BK-B',actorId:'fin@pawspace.in',reason:'backdated invoice after close'})
E) postJournal(db,{groupKey:'LATE-1',entryDate:'2026-07-15',periodCode:'2026-07',sourceType:'manual',sourceId:'X',narration:'late posting into a locked period',lines:[{accountCode:'6100-Other Expenses (1)',debit:50000},{accountCode:'1010-Bank',credit:50000}]})
F) mutateSittingFinance({bookingId:'BK-B',action:'prepare_settlement',...})
G) closeMonth(db,{period:'2026-07',...}) a second time.
d1_before:
finance_close_periods: {period_code:'2026-07', status:'locked', locked_by:'founder@pawspace.in', locked_at:1787655276838, checklist_json=[6 items all ok:true]}.
finance_monthly_closes: {period:'2026-07', status:'closed', snapshot_json.revenue={bookings:15000,bookingCount:2,total:15000}}.
canonical_bookings: BK-A status='confirmed' total_amount=10000 scheduled_start='2026-07-10T09:00:00.000Z'; BK-B status='confirmed' total_amount=5000 same window. booking_payments both 'captured'.
booking_invoices: 1 row SIT-BLR-26-27-000001 (BK-A) gross 10000 tax 1525.42.
sitting_refund_ledger: 0 rows. finance_journal_entries: 0 rows.
d1_after:
canonical_bookings: BK-A status='cancelled' (moved out of the closed month's recognised revenue AFTER the month was locked); BK-B unchanged.
sitting_refund_ledger: 1 row {id:'1178dfbc-c9d3-4a43-b60b-55bfb12c6d03', amount:10000, status:'sandbox_recorded', reference:'LATE-0001'} - a refund belonging to a locked month.
booking_invoices: 2 rows - SIT-BLR-26-27-000001 (10000/1525.42) and the NEW SIT-BLR-26-27-000002 (BK-B, gross 5000, tax 762.71, issued_at 1787655276842) issued after the lock.
finance_journal_entries: 2 rows - JRN-LATE-1-1 {entry_date:'2026-07-15', account_code:'6100-Other Expenses (1)', debit:50000, period_code:'2026-07', posted:1} and JRN-LATE-1-2 {account_code:'1010-Bank', credit:50000, period_code:'2026-07', posted:1}. Both carry the LOCKED period_code.
finance_close_periods still status='locked'; nothing recorded that the period was written into after lock.
repeatable: Yes - the probe was run twice end to end from a clean in-memory D1 with identical results.
canonical_failure: closeMonth writes finance_close_periods.status='locked' but the only code path that reads that row is closeMonth itself (plus lib/gst-accounting.ts and lib/people-finance-integration.ts, which govern a different module's tables), so refunds, service invoices and finance_journal_entries postings dated inside a closed period are accepted with no lock check whatsoever.
contributing_controls: lib/finance-accounts.ts postJournal has no period argument check and no lock lookup at all - it is the shared posting helper for wallet, revenue-recognition and cash-flow.
lib/sitting-invoice.ts / boarding / walking / taxi / grooming issue*Invoice never consult finance_close_periods.
lib/*-finance-governance.ts refund paths never consult finance_close_periods.
lib/gst-accounting.ts DOES have a locked(db,date) helper reading the same table - the control exists, it is simply not applied to the service-side money paths.
blast_radius: Every figure published from a closed month is provisional. GST returns, board-approved management accounts, statutory packages and the P&L for any locked period can all be contradicted by writes made after the lock, silently and by any actor with finance.manage. Combined with W2-08-F03 the two published surfaces for the same closed month already disagree.
regression: tests/ptja-w2-finance-regressions.test.mjs :: "W2-FIN-02: a locked period accepts no journal posting" + "W2-FIN-02: a journal cannot be labelled with a period it is not dated in" + "W2-FIN-02: an open period still posts, and a correction still lands in the next open month" + "W2-FIN-05: operational finance records cannot be dated into a closed month"
fix_note: postJournal now reads finance_close_periods and refuses any journal dated into a locked month, with the remedy closeMonth's own refusal already prescribes - post corrections in the next open period. The period is the month the entry is DATED in, so the lock cannot be walked round by relabelling, and a missing finance_close_periods table means no period was ever closed rather than an open door. All four existing callers already derived periodCode from their own entryDate. The operational paths are pinned as date-less so a later change that adds a caller-supplied date is caught rather than assumed harmless.
finding_correction: CORRECTION to this finding, on re-measurement: cases A-D were recorded as a 'late refund' and a 'backdated invoice' posted INTO the locked month. Nothing was backdated. issueSittingInvoice takes {bookingId, reason, actorId} and stamps issued_at=Date.now(); mutateSittingFinance's input type carries no accounting date at all (requestedStart/requestedEnd are SERVICE dates, not accounting dates) and its refund ledger row is created at now. Those records land in the period they actually happened in, which is the correct treatment for an operational event following a close - and since W2-08-F04 the invoice's tax now reaches that OPEN month's GST output rather than being lost. The real exposure was case E, the manual journal, because postJournal takes an explicit entryDate that can be backdated. No finance policy decision is needed after all; the earlier PARTIALLY FIXED status and its request for a policy call are withdrawn.

title: The closed month's published snapshot and the live P&L for the same month disagree by 10,000 with no reconciliation and no warning
actor: Finance viewer (finance.view) reading two governed surfaces for the same locked period: lib/finance-monthly-close.ts monthlyCloseView('2026-07') and lib/pnl-reporting.ts generatePnlReport({fromMonth:'2026-07',toMonth:'2026-07'}).
request:
After 2026-07 was closed and locked (see W2-08-F02) and a late refund cancelled BK-A (10000) inside that locked period:
monthlyCloseView(db,{period:'2026-07',actorId:'fin@pawspace.in'})
generatePnlReport(db,{fromMonth:'2026-07',toMonth:'2026-07'})
response:
monthlyCloseView => status 'closed', revenue {bookings:15000, bookingCount:2, foodOrders:0, total:15000}, gst {outputTax:0, eligibleInputTax:0, netPayable:0, invoiceCount:0}, checklist item revenue_reconciled ok:true value 15000.
generatePnlReport => totalTurnoverAmount 5000, totalExpensesAmount 50000, nettProfitAmount -45000, dataSource 'platform_live'.
d1_before: canonical_bookings for 2026-07: BK-A total_amount=10000 status='confirmed', BK-B total_amount=5000 status='confirmed'. Both surfaces would have read 15000.
d1_after: canonical_bookings: BK-A status='cancelled', BK-B status='confirmed'. finance_monthly_closes.snapshot_json.revenue.total is frozen at 15000; generatePnlReport recomputes live and excludes cancelled, returning 5000. sitting_refund_ledger holds 10000 'sandbox_recorded' which NEITHER surface reports. finance_journal_entries holds 50000 of debit which ONLY the P&L reports (the close snapshot's revenue/gst do not read the journal at all).
canonical_failure: monthlyCloseView returns the frozen snapshot for a closed period while generatePnlReport recomputes the same month live from canonical_bookings, so any post-close mutation makes the two published figures for one locked month differ permanently, and neither surface reports the refund ledger.
contributing_controls: lib/pnl-reporting.ts derives revenue from canonical_bookings.total_amount WHERE status NOT IN ('cancelled','draft') and never reads any refund ledger or contra-revenue account, so a refund is expressed only as the disappearance of the whole booking rather than as a refund line.
lib/finance-monthly-close.ts monthlyCloseView returns stored.snapshot_json verbatim once status='closed' and never re-checks it against source data or flags drift.

The two surfaces also use different exclusion sets: the close excludes status IN ('cancelled','refunded'); the P&L excludes ('cancelled','draft'). A booking left in status 'refunded' counts as revenue in the P&L and not in the close.
blast_radius: Any consumer comparing the board-approved close pack against the P&L for the same month sees two different revenue numbers and cannot tell which is authoritative. Partial refunds are invisible on both surfaces: a booking refunded in part keeps its full total_amount in the P&L and its full total in the close snapshot.
regression: tests/ptja-w2-finance-regressions.test.mjs :: "W2-FIN-06: the P&L publishes the frozen close figure alongside its own for a locked month" + "W2-FIN-06: a range with no closed month is unchanged"
fix_note: generatePnlReport now carries a closedPeriods array: for every closed or locked month in range it publishes the frozen snapshot's turnover, its own live recomputation, and the difference between them, and dataSource becomes platform_live_with_closed_periods so a consumer can see which kind of figure it is reading. The authority question is answered by the platform's own declaration: closeMonth freezes the snapshot and refuses a second close with 'post corrections in the next open period', so for a locked month the snapshot is the board-approved figure. A report with no closed month in range is unchanged.
deliberately_not_changed: The live numbers themselves. Whether a cancellation recorded in August should retroactively remove revenue from a locked July - the underlying revenue-recognition question - is a finance policy matter, and silently overwriting either figure would hide exactly the disagreement this exposes. Both are published side by side and labelled. Also unchanged: partial refunds remain invisible on both surfaces (a partly refunded booking keeps its full total_amount in each), which is recorded here and carried forward rather than resolved.

title: GST output tax at monthly close is structurally zero: the close reads finance_invoices while every service invoice writes booking_invoices, and the zero is reported as a green checklist item
actor: Finance staff (finance.manage) issuing invoices via lib/sitting-invoice.ts; founder closing the month via lib/finance-monthly-close.ts. Not preview.
request: saveSittingTaxPolicy({cityId:'blr',taxMode:'inclusive',taxRate:18,effectiveFrom:'2026-04-01',...}) then issueSittingInvoice for BK-A (total 10000) and BK-B (total 5000), then monthlyCloseView(db,{period:'2026-07',...}) and closeMonth(db,{period:'2026-07',...}).
d1_before: booking_invoices empty; finance_invoices does not exist in this environment (lib/finance-monthly-close.ts safeFirst swallows the missing-table error and returns null, which becomes 0).
d1_after:
booking_invoices: 2 rows carrying 1525.42 + 762.71 = 2288.13 of output tax.
finance_invoices: still absent/empty.
finance_monthly_closes.snapshot_json.gst = {outputTax:0, eligibleInputTax:0, netPayable:0, invoiceCount:0}, frozen into the locked close.
canonical_failure: monthlyCloseView computes output GST from `SELECT SUM(tax_total) FROM finance_invoices` (written only by the separate B2B lib/gst-accounting.ts module) while all five service invoice modules (sitting/boarding/walking/taxi/grooming-invoice.ts) write tax_amount into booking_invoices, and the safeFirst wrapper turns the missing table into 0 rather than an error, so an absent source reads as a satisfied 'gst_computed' check.
contributing_controls: safeFirst() in lib/finance-monthly-close.ts catches every SQL error and returns null; Number(null||0) = 0. A table that does not exist is indistinguishable from a month with no invoices.
The checklist item gst_computed is hardcoded ok:true regardless of the value, so no amount of missing data can block a close.
invoiceCount:0 is reported next to two real invoices, and nothing cross-checks it against booking_invoices.
blast_radius: Every monthly close publishes GST output tax and GSTR-3B net payable as 0 for the entire service business. The board approves and locks the month on that number, and lib/gst-accounting.ts's statutory package for the same period is built from finance_tax_ledger, which the service invoice path also never writes.
regression: tests/ptja-w2-finance-regressions.test.mjs :: "W2-FIN-04: service invoice tax reaches the monthly close's GST output" + "W2-FIN-04: B2B and service invoices sum, and neither is double counted" + "W2-FIN-04: an invoice outside the month, or cancelled, does not count"
fix_note: The close now reads BOTH output-tax sources: finance_invoices (written only by the B2B module lib/gst-accounting.ts) and booking_invoices.tax_amount (written by all five service invoice modules - sitting, boarding, walking, taxi, grooming). The two tables are disjoint, so their tax sums and nothing is double counted; period and cancellation filters match the existing source's. No tax rule is invented - each invoice's own tax_amount, computed by the module that issued it, is simply included in the total the close publishes.
residual_risk: lib/gst-accounting.ts's statutory package for the same period is built from finance_tax_ledger, which the service invoice path also never writes. That is a separate surface from the monthly close fixed here and was not re-measured; it is carried forward in the deferred backlog.

title: Period lock on payroll posting is bypassed by declaring a different period: the caller supplies period_code, the entry_date comes from the run, and the P&L buckets by entry_date - so 430,000 of expense lands in a locked month
actor: Finance staff, real workspace forwarded identity, role 'finance' (finance.manage / payroll.manage). Reached through POST /api/people-finance with body {action:'post_payroll_journal', runId, periodCode} - periodCode is entirely caller-supplied (app/api/people-finance/route.ts line 12: periodCode:text(body.periodCode)). Not preview.
request:
Setup: six people_finance_account_mappings configured; payroll_runs RUN-JUL with period_start=2026-07-01, period_end=2026-07-31, status='approved'; one employee_payroll_results row (gross 400000, deductions 40000, reimbursements 10000, employer_cost 20000, net_pay 370000); finance_close_periods row {period_code:'2026-07', status:'locked'}.
1) postPayrollJournal(db,{runId:'RUN-JUL',periodCode:'2026-07',actorId:'fin@pawspace.in'})  (honest period)
2) postPayrollJournal(db,{runId:'RUN-JUL',periodCode:'2026-08',actorId:'fin@pawspace.in'})  (declared open period)
3) generatePnlReport(db,{fromMonth:'2026-07',toMonth:'2026-07'}) and the same for 2026-08
d1_before: finance_close_periods: {period_code:'2026-07', status:'locked', locked_by:'founder@pawspace.in'}. finance_journal_entries: 0 rows. people_payroll_finance_posts: 0 rows.
d1_after:
finance_journal_entries: 6 rows, ALL with entry_date='2026-07-31' (derived from payroll_runs.period_end) and ALL with period_code='2026-08' (the caller's declared value):
  PAYJRN-E05F4C74-24F-1 6150-Salary and Remuneration (1) debit 400000 period_code 2026-08 entry_date 2026-07-31
  PAYJRN-E05F4C74-24F-2 6100-Other Expenses (1)         debit  10000 period_code 2026-08 entry_date 2026-07-31
  PAYJRN-E05F4C74-24F-3 6150-Salary and Remuneration (2) debit  20000 period_code 2026-08 entry_date 2026-07-31
  PAYJRN-E05F4C74-24F-4 2300-Statutory Payable   credit  40000 period_code 2026-08 entry_date 2026-07-31
  PAYJRN-E05F4C74-24F-5 2310-Net Pay Payable     credit 370000 period_code 2026-08 entry_date 2026-07-31
  PAYJRN-E05F4C74-24F-6 2320-Employer Cost Payable credit 20000 period_code 2026-08 entry_date 2026-07-31
SUM(debit)=430000, SUM(credit)=430000 (the journal itself is internally balanced).
people_payroll_finance_posts: {payroll_run_id:'RUN-JUL', period_code:'2026-08', total_debit:430000, total_credit:430000, status:'posted_uat'}.
finance_close_periods 2026-07 still status='locked' with no record that it was written into.
repeatable: Yes - run twice from a clean in-memory D1; the honest call fails with period_locked and the relabelled call succeeds both times.
canonical_failure: assertPeriodOpen() validates the caller-supplied period_code while the journal rows' entry_date is derived independently from payroll_runs.period_end, so relabelling the period in the request body posts the identical journal into a locked month, and because lib/pnl-reporting.ts buckets expenses by monthKey(entry_date) the money appears in the locked month while every period_code-keyed report puts it in the open one.
contributing_controls: lib/people-finance-integration.ts postPayrollJournal: `await assertPeriodOpen(db,input.periodCode)` runs before the run is even loaded; the run's own period is never compared to the declared one.
createSandboxStatutoryExport and recordSandboxBankReconciliation take periodCode from the same caller-supplied field and gate on it the same way.

lib/pnl-reporting.ts buckets journal debits by entry_date; lib/gst-accounting.ts generateAccountingExport, lib/cash-flow-statement.ts and lib/finance-intelligence-governance.ts all key on period_code. The two dimensions are never reconciled, so this single posting is simultaneously in July (P&L) and in August (exports, cash flow, intelligence).
blast_radius: Any actor with payroll.manage can post arbitrary payroll expense into any locked month by naming an open one, and can also silently move payroll cost between months. Independently of the lock bypass, EVERY payroll posting whose declared period_code differs from its entry_date month splits the books: the accounting export for a period (SELECT ... WHERE period_code=?) omits entries the P&L for that period includes.
regression: tests/ptja-w2-finance-regressions.test.mjs :: "W2-FIN-01: a locked payroll period cannot be written into by declaring an open one" + "W2-FIN-01: a payroll journal's declared period must agree with the dates it posts" + "W2-FIN-01: an honest posting into an open period still works, and still balances" + "W2-FIN-01: the sandbox statutory export cannot be labelled with a period the run is not dated in"
fix_note: A payroll journal's period is derived, not declared: the entries are dated from the run's own period_end, so a declared period_code that disagrees with those dates is refused (period_mismatch) and the lock is then checked against the period the money actually lands in. This closes both halves - the lock bypass and, independently of any lock, the books-split where a period_code-keyed export omits entries the entry_date-bucketed P&L includes. The same shape was then MEASURED and closed in createSandboxStatutoryExport, which stamped a July run's payload as an August statutory export. No policy is invented and no side is chosen: a genuine cross-period payroll is refused and left to a human.
collateral: tests/people-finance-integration.test.mjs is source_contract only, and its case 'Finance period locks gate employee expense links payroll journals statutory exports and reconciliations' passed for the whole life of this bypass - the string it pins was present while the control it names was walkable. The new file executes the module.
